scores.notes: Closest to the live brand: Satisfy h2s, square-edged full-bleed photos, alternating cream, white and navy bands, and the uppercase place-name pattern. Its contrast maths is the most rigorous of the three. It correctly says a .55 scrim gives only about 4.2:1 and requires .65 or more where text sits. I checked: gold on navy is 5.90:1. Motion is well disciplined. The hero settle is 4.8 s and plays once, so it stays under WCAG 2.2.2. Only one element moves on its own at a time. The ribbon switches to a still, swipeable row on keyboard focus, so a focused tile is never hidden off screen (2.4.11). The duplicate ribbon list is inert. The 390 menu is a native dialog. The AI label stays in the header (AA-805/819). Tokens are split correctly: shared candidates get --aa-*, TripPlanner-only ones get --tp-*. Risks: the home hero at 86svh / 820 px is large, so its LCP depends entirely on lib/heroes.ts serving final CDN URLs. The magazine grid and the uppercase 96 px place names are extra layout work. Tour heroes still pay the 302 hop until CIS returns final URLs. About 3 of its 6 slices are realistic this week.

Best for conversion. Gold primary and Ask-an-advisor secondary buttons are on screen at both 390 and 1440. A Ways-in trio sits under the hero. The navy CTA band adds reassurances such as 'No payment to send a draft'. On mobile, the sticky bar gives Customise and Ask an advisor half the width each. It has the strongest LCP plan for home: a curated static AVIF/WebP hero in public/hero with an art-directed portrait crop and a preload. Destination and tour heroes use a server-side resolvePhotoUrl(). Satisfy uses display: optional, which avoids layout shift. It fixes muted to #5A6270, which it shows is needed on sand. Flaws: (1) a .55 scrim gives about 4.2:1 for white text over white, not the claimed 4.7:1, so its rule for text on photos is not AA-safe. (2) The 16 s Ken Burns zoom starts by itself and runs past 5 s, so WCAG 2.2.2 would require a pause control. (3) The ribbon only pauses on :focus-within instead of switching to a still row, so a focused tile can stay translated off screen. (4) At 390 the nav links are hidden and there is no menu. (5) The featured carousel adds JS and role-description semantics that the bar does not require. Its brand look is softer (rounded corners, extra sand surface) and less like adventure.asia.

The most distinctive concept. The plan card in the hero plus a self-drawing route is a strong pull towards /plan, and the h1 as LCP on home is good for performance. It drifts from the brand: there is no photo hero on home, while adventure.asia and Nghiệp's request centre on full-width photos. It moves the AI pill to the footer, which conflicts with the AA-805/819 visible-disclosure rule. It puts every TripPlanner-only map token under --aa-*, which conflicts with ADR 0016. Its own rule says never animate the LCP element, yet it gives the destination hero a Ken Burns zoom. It is not feasible this week. It needs: a Natural Earth SVG generator; route projection; Web-Mercator maths to line up an SVG layer with Mapbox static images (2 px tolerance plus a unit test); scroll-spy on the tour page; and per-country silhouette paths. It also has about 18 animations. Good parts worth grafting: the marquee duration computed on the server, the rule that fills the strip to 2400 px, a ribbon photo variant with no gap and no radius (identical to the brand banner), the edge fade mask, a tokens.test.ts that bans raw px/hex/duration values, turning transitions off during a theme switch (M18), a :lang(vi) fallback for Satisfy, and route/pin tokens checked for 3:1 non-text contrast.

graft:
Build on "Field Journal" (immersive) and graft in the following.

From warm-clean:
(1) Home LCP: a curated static hero in public/hero/ — AVIF and WebP at 640–2560 w, a <picture> with an art-directed portrait crop below 768 px, and a React preload() with fetchpriority=high. This is safer than serving a CDN URL from heroes.ts for the biggest hero. Keep heroes.ts for the destination pages.
(2) Phase 1: a server-side resolvePhotoUrl() (fetch with redirect: 'manual', read the Location header, cache with ISR) for the destination and tour hero images, until CIS returns final URLs.
(3) Satisfy with display: 'optional', so the script face never causes a swap shift.
(4) The "Ways in" trio under the search card (Find by destination / Explore on the map / Start from a tour), using the brand -color.svg icons.
(5) The navy CTA band copy: three reassurances (real Adventure Asia tours / change days and stops yourself / no payment to send a draft), plus a gold "Plan my trip" button and an outline "Ask an advisor" button.
(6) The mobile sticky tour bar split 50/50 between "Customise" and "Ask an advisor", with padding for env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
(7) muted set to #5A6270 (needed on sand, and it matches CIS AA-760).
(8) A 1 px --aa-line border on navy bands in dark mode, so they read apart from bg.
(9) prefetch={false} on the footer legal links.
(10) Keep 1 px borders on buttons and chips for forced-colours (Windows High Contrast) mode.
(11) The AA-812 "Photo: {cover_place}" caption on cards whose cover does not come from the tour.

From map-first:
(1) Work out the marquee duration on the server: n × (tile + gap) / speed, written inline per breakpoint. No JS measuring.
(2) The fill rule: repeat the item set until one copy is at least 2400 px wide. Later repeats are aria-hidden, and the same photo never sits next to itself. This removes immersive's "animate only when n ≥ 10" limit.
(3) A ribbon "photos" variant with no gap and no radius on the destination page, so it matches the brand banner exactly. Add a 48 px edge fade mask.
(4) lib/tokens.test.ts, which bans text-[NNpx], raw hex values and raw duration-/ease- classes in app/ and components/site/.
(5) Turn transitions off for one frame during a theme switch (data-theme-switching).
(6) A :lang(vi) fallback from Satisfy to Poppins 600.
(7) Later slices only: --tp-route, --tp-route-casing and pin tokens, checked for at least 3:1 against the land they sit on (for /plan), and day discs on the tour timeline that match the map pins.

Corrections to keep:
- Immersive's rule that text on photos sits only where the scrim is .65 or darker (warm-clean's .55 fails). Warm-clean's 16 s Ken Burns is not adopted; keep immersive's 4.8 s settle, once.
- The AI label stays in the header. Do not take map-first's move to the footer.
- TripPlanner-only tokens use the --tp-* prefix (ADR 0016).
- The SVG Asia map hero and the Mapbox SVG overlay are deferred as their own later issue.
